title: Introduce token saliency smokecheck and CI soft-fail adapter
author: Priya Kapoor
release_notes: Add token-level saliency smokecheck and a CI adapter that soft-fails noisy regressions to reduce noise during rollout. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Summary: Add a new token-level saliency smokecheck that detects sudden shifts in token attribution patterns for prompt sets, plus a CI soft-fail adapter that lets teams ship the check gated as a warning for the first rollout window. Motivation: high-sensitivity prompt regressions can be noisy in early adoption; teams want early detection of quality regressions (token attribution drift) without failing pipelines for harmless distribution shifts. This PR implements a conservative detector and a CI adapter that records findings as annotations and optionally converts failures to warnings for a configurable grace period.

What changed (high-level):
- eval_harness/smokechecks/token_saliency.py: new smokecheck implementing token-level attribution fingerprints, baseline snapshot loader, and drift score computation. The algorithm computes per-token average saliency vectors across a prompt cohort and reports Jensen-Shannon divergence aggregated to prompt-level and cohort-level signals. Includes configurable sampling and smoothing to avoid noisy single-run spikes.
- eval_harness/ci/soft_fail_adapter.py: CI adapter that integrates with the existing eval CI pipeline; it inspects smokecheck outputs and, if the check is in 'soft' mode, converts non-critical failures to annotations and a non-blocking status. Soft mode is time-bounded and respects team-level whitelists.
- tests/test_token_saliency.py: unit tests for saliency computation, small synthetic prompts with deterministic saliency maps, edge cases (zero-length token sequences), and missing attribution entries.
- ci/workflows/eval-smokechecks.yml: add step to run the token saliency smokecheck and conditionally trigger soft-fail behavior based on repo config file.
- docs/smokechecks/token-saliency.md: short design doc and migration notes for teams enabling the check.
- examples/prompt_sets/saliency-demo.jsonl: small prompt cohort used in integration test and demo runbook.

Commits (summary):
- c1b3f8d: initial token_saliency module with core saliency fingerprint logic and tests
- a2d4f9b: add CI adapter + workflow integration and configuration parsing
- f7e9b2a: tighten vector normalization, add smoothing kernel and sampling harness
- be4d2ca: docs, examples, and fix edge-case tests; update changelog

Design notes / algorithm:
- We treat attribution maps as token-anchored score vectors; for each prompt in a cohort we normalize token scores by L1 and compute a distribution over token positions. The detector computes an empirical distribution over positions aggregated across the cohort and compares current-run distribution to the saved baseline via JS divergence.
- To avoid spurious alerts from short runs, the smokecheck requires minimum cohort size and a median-token-length threshold. Low-signal cohorts are skipped and annotated with a reason.
- The detector exposes tunables: cohort_window, sample_fraction, smoothing_alpha, and js_threshold. Default values are conservative (higher threshold, stronger smoothing) to prioritize precision over recall on first rollout.

Testing and QA:
- Unit tests cover normalization, divergence calc, and guard rails for missing/zero attributions.
- Integration test runs the workflow against examples/prompt_sets/saliency-demo.jsonl in CI matrix (small/medium cohorts).
- Local manual runs validated behavior across three baseline snapshots (stable, drifted, and adversarial). Results recorded in the PR artifacts.

CI behavior and incidents:
- Initial CI run (2024-11-16) showed one flaky test in tests/test_token_saliency.py on macOS runner (timing-dependent). Flake traced to async RNG seeding; added deterministic seeding in f7e9b2a and retried.
- Soft-fail adapter enabled in repo config for the first two weeks of rollout; by default it annotates failures and does not block merges. A follow-up job (ENG-1210) will flip enforcement after verification.

Review thread (highlights):
- Diego Marques: "Thanks — solid design. A few asks: add explicit overflow protections in JS divergence impl and ensure the adapter respects override flags from repo config." (addressed in a2d4f9b and be4d2ca)
- Asha Raman: "Can we expose a debug-mode to emit per-prompt token heatmaps to artifacts? That would be useful for triage." (added optional debug artifact; gated by env var)
- Samir Patel: "We should not rely on attribution format being dense arrays; added a comment to normalize sparse inputs." (handled in normalization helper)
- Author (Priya): replied inline to each comment and pushed fixes. Final approval from Diego and Asha.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main with soft-fail adapter turned on for the org default config (non-blocking).
2) Monitor annotated findings via the eval console dashboard for 14 days (metric: percent cohorts flagged, median JS divergence).
3) Triage top 20 flagged prompts/week, tune js_threshold and smoothing_alpha accordingly.
4) Flip adapter to blocking after ENG-1210 verifies signal quality or extend soft window if noisy.

Backward compatibility and impact:
- No breaking changes to public SDKs or API surfaces. The smokecheck is opt-in via repo config. Teams not opting-in will see no changes.

Notes for release notes:
- Introduces a conservative token-level saliency smokecheck to detect attribution drift across prompt cohorts. Includes a CI soft-fail adapter to reduce noise during initial rollout.

Additional pointers:
- Linear: ENG-1182 (detector prototype), ENG-1210 (rollout & enforcement runbook)
- Design doc: docs/smokechecks/token-saliency.md

Merge: Squash merged by Diego Marques on 2024-11-21 after CI green and approvals.
